messages.content:
You write the two short notices Ryde sends after a dispute ruling: one to the rider, one to the driver.
Each ≤ 120 words, plain English, second person, no legalese: state the outcome, the one or two facts that decided it,
the amount and how it is paid (Ryde voucher), and what it means for the recipient (e.g. account review). Do not cite
ids like F3 or RD-2. If the case was escalated to a human reviewer, say only that and what the reviewer will look at —
do not state a conclusion and do not promise a timeframe (the routing notice carries the service level). Return JSON: {"rider": "...", "driver": "..."}

Case B-0026. Final outcome: refund_full, amount $6.61 as a Ryde voucher. Account flag: yes. Recommended action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) and send the driver's account to Ryde review for a fake arrival confirmation + flag_account.
Reasoning:
The driver cancelled this RydeX trip and kept the $6.61 cancellation fee on the ground that the rider was a no-show [F3][F6]. Under NS-0 the case therefore enters through NS-1/NS-2 [F3][NS-0]. NS-1 requires all three elements: an arrival confirmation, GPS placing the driver at the pickup point at the moment of the tap, and a continuous wait of more than 3 minutes inside the pickup radius until cancelling [F5][F4][NS-1]. Only the first element is satisfied — the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:06:15 [F5][NS-1]. On the second, the tap was made 600 m from the pickup point, the driver's closest approach in the whole trip was 599 m, and the platform never recorded him at the pickup point [F5][F1][F4][NS-1]. On the third, he spent 0 s continuously within 200 m of the pickup after the tap, far short of the 180 s threshold, though he sat stationary 600 m away from 12:05:55 to 12:09:25 [F5][F2][NS-1]. NS-1 (ii) and (iii) therefore both fail, and NS-2 requires the $6.61 to be refunded in full [F5][F1][F3][NS-1][NS-2]. The chat confirms the rider was actually at the pickup point while the driver asserted he was "here already" from elsewhere [F8][F9][F10]. Because the driver pressed the arrival button while GPS showed him outside the pickup range, the case additionally carries a flag_account action under NS-2 [F5][F1][NS-2]. The refund is a single fixed item of $6.61 taken from the fare record, so the amount is $6.61, not a per-km computation [F3][F6][NS-2], and is issued as a Ryde voucher under NS-7 [NS-7]. The traffic and weather records (band 3 on Jalan Besar, no incidents, fair weather) are irrelevant to a no-show case and do not explain the driver's position [F13][F14][F15]. The driver's written statement that he pressed "I'm Here" and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup is a claim contradicted by the GPS and timeline records, which prevail [F12][F3][F5][NS-1].

function.name: final_result
function.description: The final response which ends this conversation

function.name: final_result
function.arguments: {"rider": "We reviewed your dispute and you're getting the $6.61 cancellation fee refunded in full. It's paid as a Ryde voucher, not cash. Two facts decided it: the driver tapped \"I'm Here\" while he was still around 600 m from your pickup point, and he never actually waited inside the pickup area for the required time after that tap. Your chat also shows you were at the pickup point. The driver's account is being sent to Ryde review. Nothing else is needed from you.", "driver": "We reviewed the cancellation dispute on this trip. The $6.61 cancellation fee is being refunded to the rider as a Ryde voucher. Two facts decided it: your \"I'm Here\" tap was made about 600 m from the pickup point, and you did not spend the required continuous time inside the pickup area after tapping. Your account is being sent to Ryde review for the arrival confirmation. This may affect your ability to keep trip earnings in similar cases, so please make sure your arrival taps match your actual location."}
